definition: A software platform that allows users to build, train, or deploy AI models and applications through visual interfaces rather than writing code directly.
details: No-code AI platforms lower the barrier to building AI-powered applications, enabling domain experts without deep programming or ML expertise to prototype and deploy models or workflows.

explainer.lead: A no-code AI platform lets users build, train or deploy AI models and applications through visual interfaces instead of writing code. It matters because it lowers the barrier for domain experts without deep programming or ML expertise.

tiers.eli5: It's a tool where you drag and click to make an AI app instead of writing programming code.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers and domain experts use these platforms to prototype and deploy models or workflows quickly. A pitfall is that avoiding code can cap how far a workflow can be customized or tuned.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a software platform for building, training or deploying AI models and applications via visual interfaces rather than direct coding; no formal limits are specified.

explainer.example: A domain expert could assemble a visual workflow that trains and deploys a model without writing any code.
